spark.scene: True-color satellite view of the main Hawaiian Islands from Kauai in the northwest to Hawaii in the southeast. Scattered white cumulus and cirrus clouds cover portions of the islands and surrounding ocean, with a large clear dark-ocean area in the central and south-central region and a band of white clouds to the south. The Island of Hawaii is partly cloudy with white clouds along the west and south coasts and a dark brown land surface visible in the southeast. No distinct gray, brown, or bluish haze, smoke, or volcanic plume separate from ordinary clouds is clearly visible.

classify.caveats: No plume found; nothing to classify.

kilauea.activity_summary: The Halema'uma'u eruption of Kīlauea is currently paused after episode 55 fountaining ended on October 17. Summit reinflation continues today. Overview: The summit eruption of Kīlauea in Halemaʻumaʻu is paused following 5.7 hours of lava fountaining during episode 55 on October 17, 2026.

mauna_loa.activity_summary: Mauna Loa earthquake counts decreased in September compared to August, and minor inflation continues. Mauna Loa had a decrease in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 53 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the September reporting period, after 87 in August. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks.
